PLU1#0.quote: Ludhiana was founded in 1480 as Lodhi-ana, named after the Lodhi dynasty that established it.

PLU1#1.quote: Situated on the banks of the Sutlej River, it is the most populous city in Punjab and has earned the title of the Manchester of India for its dominance in manufacturing and export of woollen garments, hosiery goods, cycle parts, machine components, sewing machines, and mopeds.

PLU2#0.quote: Ludhiana is acclaimed for its Tandoori cuisine, cooked in huge earthen ovens buried half in the ground with a coal fire below.

PLU2#1.quote: The Kila Raipur Sports Festival, held annually near Ludhiana every February, is known as India's Rural Olympics.

PLU2#2.quote: It began in 1933 when philanthropist Inder Singh Grewal envisioned an annual gathering where farmers could test their physical endurance.

PLU3#0.quote: How to Reach By Air: Ludhiana Airport (Halwara Airport) serves the city directly. Shaheed Bhagat Singh International Airport, Chandigarh (Mohali), and Sri Guru Ram Dass Jee International Airport, Amritsar, are the two international airports closest to Ludhiana.

PLU3#1.quote: By Train: Ludhiana Junction Railway Station is one of the major railway junctions on the Northern Railway network, with direct connections to Delhi, Amritsar, Chandigarh, and other major cities.

PLU3#2.quote: By Road: Ludhiana ISBT (Amar Shaheed Sukhdev Interstate Bus Terminal) is the main road transport hub, well connected by PRTC and private services to all major cities in Punjab and neighbouring states.

PLU3#3.quote: Local Transport: Auto-rickshaws, shared vehicles, and city buses operate within Ludhiana city and between towns in the district.

PLU4#0.quote: February is the best time to attend the Kila Raipur Rural Olympics.

PLU6#0.quote: Ludhiana district gave India three martyrs whose names are central to the story of Indian resistance to British rule: Shaheed Kartar Singh Sarabha, Shaheed Sukhdev Thapar, and Lala Lajpat Rai.

PLU6#1.quote: Makki di Roti with Sarson da Saag is the winter staple found at dhabas and households across the district.

PLU5#0.quote: Hotels in the Area: Radisson Blu Hotel

PJL1#0.quote: Jalandhar is believed to be the oldest city in Punjab, with its history stretching across Harappan, Vedic, Mauryan, Gupta, and Mughal periods.

PJL1#1.quote: A third account derives the name from the vernacular term meaning 'area inside the water', a reference to its position between the rivers Sutlej and Beas, alongside the historic Grand Trunk Road.

PJL1#2.quote: Jalandhar served as the capital of Punjab following the Partition of 1947 before the administrative headquarters shifted to Shimla and then to Chandigarh.

PJL1#3.quote: Today, Jalandhar is the largest city in the Doaba region and a hub of sports goods manufacturing, with products exported to countries across the world.

PJL2#0.quote: Devi Talab Mandir is one of India's 51 Shakti Pithas. In Jalandhar, the presiding goddess is known as Tripurmalini, and the right breast of Goddess Sati is believed to have fallen at this site.

PJL2#1.quote: The Harballabh Sangeet Sammelan, held annually in December at Devi Talab Mandir, is the oldest Hindustani classical music festival in the country.

PJL2#2.quote: The village of Sansarpur, in the vicinity of Jalandhar Cantonment, is known as the Nursery of Hockey Players and has produced multiple Olympians including Balbir Singh, Gurdev Singh, Tarsem Singh, Harbinder Singh, and Ajit Pal Singh.

PJL3#0.quote: A domestic airport is located at Adampur, Jalandhar, approximately 25 km from Jalandhar Bus Stand and 23 km from Jalandhar City Railway Station.

PJL3#1.quote: The second nearest airport is Sri Guru Ram Dass Jee International Airport, Amritsar, approximately 75 km northwest of Jalandhar.

PJL3#2.quote: By Road: Jalandhar City Bus Stand is the main road transport hub, with regular PRTC and private services connecting Jalandhar to major cities across Punjab, Haryana, Himachal Pradesh, and Delhi.

PJL3#3.quote: Local Transport: Auto-rickshaws, shared vehicles, and local buses operate within Jalandhar city and between towns in the district.

PJL4#0.quote: Makki di Roti with Sarson da Saag, Chole Bhature, Amritsari Kulcha, Dal Makhani, and Patiala Lassi are among the staples widely available across the city.

PJL4#1.quote: Jalandhari Fish Fry and Butter Chicken represent the city's non-vegetarian tradition.

PJL4#2.quote: Hotels in the Area: Sarovar Portico Jalandhar, Ramada Encore by Wyndham Jalandhar, Golden Tulip Jalandhar, Radisson Hotel Jalandhar

PJL4#3.quote: Best Time to Visit: October to March

PJL5#0.quote: Nurmahal, located 33 km from Jalandhar, is a town steeped in history and Mughal architecture.

PBT1#0.quote: Bathinda district lies in the Malwa region of Punjab. It is bounded by Faridkot and Moga in the north, Muktsar in the west, Barnala and Mansa in the east, and the state of Haryana in the south.

PBT1#1.quote: Bathinda is popularly known as the City of Lakes on account of its five artificial lakes. Takht Sri Damdama Sahib at Talwandi Sabo is one of the five Takhts the highest seats of temporal authority in Sikhism.

PBT1#2.quote: History & Background Bathinda is one of the oldest cities in Punjab. According to historical records cited in the Ainai-Barar Bans , the city was founded by Bhati Rao in the third century.

PBT1#3.quote: The land is a flat agricultural belt, historically part of the Lakhi Jungle region, and the district is a significant cotton and wheat producing zone.

PBT2#0.quote: The fort, which has stood since the 12th century, is maintained by the Archaeological Survey of India and has been declared the oldest surviving fort in India.

PBT2#1.quote: It is the site where Malik Ikhtiar-ud-din Altunia, the 13th-century Governor of Bathinda, rebelled and imprisoned Empress Razia Sultana, one of the most powerful rulers of the Delhi Sultanate.

PBT2#2.quote: Famously, the governor and the empress fell in love during her captivity, and went on to marry each other.

PBT2#3.quote: Razia Sultana , the first woman ruler of India, was imprisoned in Qila Mubarak in 1240 AD. The district is home to prestigious institutions including the Central University of Punjab , Maharaja Ranjit Singh Punjab Technical University , and AIIMS Bathinda .

PBT3#0.quote: How to Reach By Air: Bathinda has its own domestic airport located approximately 25–26 km from the city, with flights connecting to New Delhi and Jammu.

PBT3#1.quote: By Rail: Bathinda Junction is one of the major railway junctions in northern Punjab, situated on the Ambala–Bathinda branch line.

PBT3#2.quote: PRTC and PUNBUS services operate from Bathinda Bus Stand to cities across Punjab and neighbouring states.

PBT3#3.quote: Local Transport: Auto-rickshaws and shared tempos operate within Bathinda city and between the city and nearby attractions.

PBT4#0.quote: Best Time to Visit: October to March.

PBT4#2.quote: Food & Flavours The food of Bathinda is the food of the Malwa heartland cooked in desi ghee, built on dairy, and heavy with the flavours of wheat and mustard.

PPK1#0.quote: Pathankot is situated in the northernmost part of Punjab, where the states of Punjab, Himachal Pradesh, and Jammu & Kashmir converge.

PPK1#1.quote: Nestled in the foothills of the Shivalik Range and surrounded by the Ravi and Chakki rivers, the district serves as the gateway to the Himalayan hill destinations of Dalhousie, Dharamshala, Kangra, and Chamba.

PPK1#2.quote: With an average elevation of 332 metres and views of the snow-capped Himalayas to the north, the district is characterised by lush greenery, river valleys, and forested foothills.

PPK1#3.quote: Owing to its strategic location, Pathankot has historically been an important centre for travel, trade, and cultural exchange between the plains and the hills.

PPK2#0.quote: Pathankot is famous for its high-quality litchi production and exports its produce to countries including the UAE, France, Canada, Thailand, and Saudi Arabia.

PPK2#1.quote: The district is home to the historic Shahpurkandi Fort and is closely associated with the princely state of Nurpur.

PPK2#2.quote: Places to Visit Ranjit Sagar Dam Located near Shahpurkandi, Ranjit Sagar Dam is one of the largest hydroelectric projects in Northern India. Built on the Ravi River, the dam is surrounded by forested hills and offers panoramic views of the reservoir and the surrounding landscape.

PPK2#3.quote: The modern Atal Setu bridge has emerged as one of Punjab's most photographed tourism landmarks.

PPK3#0.quote: How to Reach By Air Pathankot is served by Pathankot Airport (IXP) , a domestic airport located approximately 3 km from the city centre and about 7 km from Pathankot Railway Station .

PPK3#1.quote: The airport operates flights connecting Pathankot with Delhi. For international and wider domestic connectivity, the nearest international airport is Sri Guru Ram Dass Jee International Airport, Amritsar , located approximately 119 km away .

PPK3#2.quote: Pathankot Cantonment Railway Station and Pathankot Junction connect the district with Delhi, Amritsar, Jammu, Chandigarh, Mumbai, Ahmedabad, Kolkata, and other major cities.

PPK3#3.quote: The district is connected by National Highways to major cities including Amritsar (110 km), Jammu (105 km), Dharamshala (85 km), Dalhousie (80 km), Kangra (95 km), and Chandigarh (250 km).

PPK4#0.quote: Best Time to Visit: October to March.

PPK4#1.quote: Spring (February–April) is especially enjoyable, while summers can be hot and monsoons receive moderate to heavy rainfall.

PTT1#0.quote: History & Background Tarn Taran was founded in 1596 by Sri Guru Arjan Dev Ji, the fifth Sikh Guru.

PTT1#1.quote: The Gurudwara holds a unique distinction among all Sikh shrines: it is home to the largest Sarovar (holy water tank) of any Gurudwara in the world, and is the only Gurudwara considered a replica of the revered Sri Harmandir Sahib, Amritsar.

PTT1#2.quote: The Gurudwara holds a unique distinction among all Sikh shrines: it is home to the largest Sarovar (holy water tank) of any Gurudwara in the world, and is the only Gurudwara considered a replica of the revered Sri Harmandir Sahib, Amritsar.

PTT2#0.quote: the full phrase means "the boat that takes one across the ocean of existence."

PTT2#1.quote: For this reason, the Sarovar has historically been known as Dukh Nivaran — the eradicator of affliction.

PTT3#0.quote: How to Reach By Air: Sri Guru Ram Dass Jee International Airport, Amritsar (IATA: ATQ) — approximately 25 km from Tarn Taran Sahib.

PTT3#1.quote: By Train: Tarn Taran has its own railway station on the Amritsar–Ferozepur line. Amritsar Junction, approximately 25 km away, is the nearest major railhead with broader national connectivity.

PTT3#2.quote: By Road: Regular PRTC and PUNBUS services run from Amritsar Bus Stand to Tarn Taran. The district connects Amritsar with the cities of the Majha region.

PTT3#3.quote: Harike Wetland, located in this district, is the largest wetland in northern India and is a designated Ramsar site.

PTT4#0.quote: Amavasya pilgrimage is active every month throughout the year.

PTT4#1.quote: Local Transport: Auto-rickshaws and shared tempos operate within Tarn Taran town and between towns in the district.

PAS1#0.quote: Anandpur Sahib, located on the left bank of the Sutlej approximately 40 km from Rupnagar town, was founded by Sri Guru Teg Bahadur Ji and is the birthplace of the Khalsa.

PAS1#1.quote: It was here that Sri Guru Gobind Singh Ji created the Khalsa on Baisakhi Day in 1699, the most significant event in the history of the Sikh faith.

PAS2#0.quote: Takht Sri Keshgarh Sahib is the principal shrine of Anandpur Sahib. This is a historic site where, on the day of Baisakhi in 1699, Sri Guru Gobind Singh Ji initiated his followers into the order of the Khalsa.

PAS2#1.quote: In the sanctum sanctorum of Takht Sri Keshgarh Sahib, a number of the belongings of Sri Guru Gobind Singh Ji are preserved- a khanda, a dagger, a shield, a chakkar, three swords and several spears.

PAS2#2.quote: Anandgarh Fort is one of the five forts built by Sri Guru Gobind Singh Ji to protect Sikhs and other residents from the Mughal Empire.

PAS2#3.quote: It is believed that the construction of this fort began in 1689 and took over a decade to complete.

PAS5#0.quote: October to March is the most comfortable season.

PAS3#0.quote: Hola Mohalla in February/March and Baisakhi in April are the most significant times to visit Anandpur Sahib.

PAS3#1.quote: At the Gurdwaras of Anandpur Sahib, particularly at Takht Sri Keshgarh Sahib, round-the-clock langar is served free to all visitors regardless of faith or background during Hola Mohalla, this langar is extended along the roads leading into the city from all directions.

PAS4#0.quote: How to Reach By Air: The nearest airport is Shaheed Bhagat Singh International Airport, Chandigarh (Mohali). Rupnagar is approximately 50 km from Chandigarh.

PAS4#1.quote: Anandpur Sahib Railway Station serves the Anandpur Sahib area directly. By Road: Regular bus services operate from Chandigarh and other major cities in Punjab to Rupnagar and Anandpur Sahib.

PAS4#2.quote: By Road: Regular bus services operate from Chandigarh and other major cities in Punjab to Rupnagar and Anandpur Sahib. Rupnagar is approximately 50 km from Chandigarh.

PAS2B#0.quote: Here, Sri Guru Gobind Singh Ji baptized five brave men with amrit (holy water).

PDS1#0.quote: One of the five sacred Takhts of Sikhism, Takht Sri Damdama Sahib is a gleaming white Gurudwara located in Talwandi Sabo (28 km from Bathinda).

PDS1#1.quote: It is the place where the tenth Sikh Guru, Sri Guru Gobind Singh Ji, took rest for nearly a year and compiled the final version of the holy Sikh scripture 'Sri Guru Granth Sahib Ji' in the year 1705.

PDS1#2.quote: Takht Sri Damdama Sahib at Talwandi Sabo is one of the five Takhts the highest seats of temporal authority in Sikhism.

PDS1#3.quote: After his fiercest battles with the Mughals at Anandpur Sahib, Chamkaur Sahib, and Muktsar, Guru Gobind Singh Ji retired to the jungles of Malwa and took rest ( Dam ) at Talwandi Sabo hence the name Damdama Sahib.

PDS2#0.quote: Large numbers of devotees visit this place to seek blessings and witness the belongings of Sri Guru Gobind Singh Ji, which include a sword, seal and a sacred mirror, stored in the premises of the Gurudwara.

PDS2#1.quote: Just 10 minutes away from Takht Sri Damdama Sahib

PDS2#2.quote: Places to Visit Takht Sri Damdama Sahib, Talwandi Sabo One of the five Takhts of Sikhism and known as Guru Ki Kashi the Banaras of the Guru.

PDU1#1.quote: The bridge provides an approach to the temple. The temple tank is 541 ft X 432 ft and 20 ft deep, which according to government records was built here in 16th century.

PDU1#2.quote: The temple tank is 541 ft X 432 ft and 20 ft deep, which according to government records was built here in 16th century.

PDU1#3.quote: Located roughly at a distance of about one and a half kilometers from the Golden Temple, Durgiana Temple is dedicated to the Hindu Goddess and is also known as the Laxmi Narayan Temple.

PDU2#0.quote: Domes of the main temple along with the upper side of the walls adjacent to it are carved with Gold.

PDU2#1.quote: 12X12 feet huge silver carved and engraved door

PDU2#2.quote: In the central GARBH GRAH inside the main temple idols of Shri Lakshmi-Narayan in the standng position and on one side of them Shri Ram Darbar and on the other side the idols of Shri Radha-Krishna Ji along with Shri Giriraj Ji Maharaj present a wonderful divine look.

PMM1#0.quote: the French inspired rose-hued mosque with a blue tiled roof known as the 'Moorish Mosque' was built in the 1930s.

PMM1#1.quote: A visit to Kapurthala is incomplete without seeing this masterpiece designed by French architect M Manteaux, with a dome richly decorated inside by a team of artists from the Mayo School of Art, Lahore.

PMM1#2.quote: The mosque is listed as a National Monument by the Archaeological Survey of India

PMM1#3.quote: It serves as a great example of the secular traditions of Punjab.

PMM2#0.quote: The district is approximately 20 km from Jalandhar, 75 km from Amritsar, 165 km from Chandigarh, and around 40 km from Sultanpur Lodhi.

PMM2#1.quote: Built in 1908 by Maharaja Jagatjit Singh, the palace is modelled on the Palace of Versailles in France and showcases remarkable Indo-Saracenic architecture.

PHW1#0.quote: Built in 1968, the Hussainiwala National Martyrs Memorial is a tribute to revolutionary heroes Shaheed Bhagat Singh, Shaheed Rajguru and Shaheed Sukhdev who were cremated there on 23rd March 1931.

PHW1#1.quote: A 'Shaheedi Mela' (Martyr's fair) takes place on 23rd March every year to commemorate the martyrdom of these freedom fighters.

PHW1#2.quote: Tourists from all corners of the world visit this well-maintained park to see the life-sized black granite statues of the three brave martyrs, standing in a pose evoking their famous slogan – “Inquilab Zindabad”.

PHW1#3.quote: A daily retreat ceremony reminiscent of the Attari-Wagah border ceremony is also held here by the Border Security Forc.

PKC1#0.quote: Sri Kartarpur Sahib Corridor which serves as vital spiritual and cultural link allowing pilgrims from India to visit Gurdwara Sri Kartarpur Sahib is situated in Narowal District of Western Punjab, Pakistan.

PKC1#1.quote: Sri Kartarpur Sahib is associated with the last eighteen years of Guru Nanak Devji where he left for heavenly abode on September 22, 1539.

PKC2#0.quote: Gurdwara Sri Kartarpur Sahib situated in Shakargarh Tehsil of District Gurdaspur became part of Pakistan as a result of Sir Cyril Radcliffe Award announced on August 17, 1947 which partitioned the District in two parts and awarded Shakargarh Tehsil to Pakistan.

PKC2#1.quote: The town of Dera Baba Nanak is situated at a distance of about 40 kms from the District Head quarters town of Gurdaspur.

PKC2#2.quote: A number of roads connect this historic town with Batala (35 km) and Amritsar (48 km). National Highway No 503 D will connect it with Jalandhar Amritsar road via Batala and Chowk Mehta.

PKC3#0.quote: The present building of Darbar Sahib Shrine at Kartarpur Sahib and residential quarters were constructed in 1911-1912. It has a symbolic platform raised in the memory of Sri Guru Nanak Devji's final resting place.

PNM1#0.quote: Nurmahal, located 33 km from Jalandhar, is a town steeped in history and Mughal architecture.

PNM1#1.quote: The town derives its name from Nur Jahan, the wife of Emperor Jahangir, who is believed to have been brought up here.

PNM1#2.quote: Built under the supervision of Zakariya Khan, the then Governor of Doab (the region of Punjab) in 1618, the serai was intended to provide a safe and comfortable stop for travellers and traders on the Lahore-Agra route.

PNM2#0.quote: The serai, in the form of a quadrangle consisting of 140 cells, is built around a large courtyard, typical of the caravanserais used during the Mughal period, which were designed to accommodate people, goods, and animals.

PNM2#1.quote: The majestic Western Gateway is made of red sandstone, and has intricate carvings depicting birds, elephants, camels, fairies and humans.

PNM2#2.quote: At the entrance to the gateway, there are inscriptions written in four rhyming verses, flanked by scenes of fighting animals and sculpted lotus mounds.
